title: Pager Sentinels: Soft-cutover Runbook and Automated Noise Attenuation for Multi-region SLO Failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see noisy paging during transient regional degradations where the SLO-based alerting fabric simultaneously fires multiple high-severity pages (frontend latency + KV-cache miss spike + queue-depth) for the same underlying capacity stress. This floods on-call, increases MTTR, and causes premature or chaotic failovers between regions.

Goal: Implement a repeatable, automated 'Pager Sentinels' pattern: lightweight, readable sentinel rules that (a) correlate signals into a single page event, (b) apply graduated attenuation (alert severity downgrades & suppression windows) based on repro frequency and SLO burn rate, and (c) perform an orchestrated soft-cutover / load-shedding playbook that minimizes cross-region oscillation. Document a clear on-call runbook and automate the first two mitigation steps so paging noise is reduced while safe failover remains available.

Scope: Engineering work to implement rule templates in our alerting system (Prometheus/Synapse -> PagerDuty), build/runbook automation playflows in the orchestrator, add observability dashboards and synthetic canaries, and ship on-call docs + training. Does NOT include wholesale redesign of SLO definitions or quota architecture (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Single correlated incident is created for grouped signals that previously created >3 separate pages during a 10m window
Pager volume for top-3 noisy alert classes reduced by >=60% during synthetic regional degradation tests
Automated attenuation rules can downgrade to a low-severity notification (Slack channel + incident log) without human intervention for transient bursts < 15 minutes
Soft-cutover sequence can be invoked automatically and manually; when invoked automatically it uses prefixed KV-cache warmup and staged traffic steering to avoid global failover oscillation
Runbook doc with step-by-step decision tree published and acknowledged by on-call rotation (2 sign-offs from SRE leads)
Telemetry dashboards show stable SLO burn-rate calculations and annotated timeline during 3 simulated failovers
design_notes: Introduce 'sentinel' abstraction: small boolean predicates that reference multiple metrics (latency p99, error rate, queue depth, cache eviction rate) and emit a sentinel signal when combinator matches
Correlation window: default 10m with exponential backoff for re-correlation to avoid re-triggering on noisy oscillation
Attenuation policy: tiered (page -> message -> silent log) based on frequency, SLO burn velocity, and active mitigations

Soft-cutover flow: (1) read-only steer to secondary region for low-priority traffic, (2) enable KV-cache prewarm if secondary, (3) gradual traffic shift via weighted routing, (4) monitor canary slices for 2x p50 latency horizon before further shift
Circuit breaker integration: combine sentinels with existing CBs to trigger granular shedding at route/route-group level, not whole region
Safety: maintain manual abort points and 1-minute human confirmation for escalations that cross the high-impact threshold
implementation_steps: 1) Map noisy alerts to candidate sentinel groups (review top 20 noisy signals from last 90 days)
2) Prototype sentinel rules in staging alerting cluster and simulate signal bursts with chaos job
3) Implement attenuation automations: escalation policies that automatically downgrade/suppress and annotate incidents
4) Integrate attenuation decisions with PagerDuty routing (use dedup key + context payload for runbook link)
5) Build soft-cutover orchestrator run: implement staged traffic steering (weights API) + KV-cache warmup hooks
6) Add dashboards: grouped-incident view, sentinel health, attenuation actions metrics, canary progress visualizer
7) Publish runbook doc and run 2 tabletop drills with on-call rotation; collect feedback and update
8) Roll out sentinel rules to prod in a 3-week canary: 25% clusters -> 50% -> 100% with telemetry gates
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive attenuation could hide true incidents. Mitigation: attenuation thresholds conservative by default, require explicit high-impact indicator to suppress pages; build audit trail of suppressed incidents
Risk: Soft-cutover could increase latency for critical customers. Mitigation: use weighted routing with canary slices and abort conditions (p99 latency increase > 20% triggers rollback)
Risk: Complexity added to on-call cognitive load. Mitigation: simplify runbook into short decision tree and provide in-console one-click escalation to full page
testing_plan: Unit tests for sentinel predicate logic and correlation windows
Integration tests: end-to-end alert -> incident generation -> attenuation action -> PagerDuty routing
Chaos runs: simulate 3 regional degradations (small, medium, large) and measure page counts & SLO burn trajectory
Load test soft-cutover routine under synthetic traffic and KV cache cold-start scenarios
Postmortem drill after tabletop: validate runbook clarity and tooling ergonomics
comments: 2026-02-12 Aisha Patel: Initial proposal drafted after reviewing recent on-call logs. Flagged memory-pressure incidents that cascaded into redundant pages.
2026-02-18 Diego Morales: Completed top-20 noisy alert mapping. Added candidate sentinel groups for 'cache storm' and 'queue backpressure'.
2026-02-22 Sanjay Rao (SRE): Suggested adding explicit customer-impact weighting to attenuation decision so critical customers trigger full page always.

2026-03-01 QA: First proto of sentinel rules deployed to staging. Observed expected correlation but attenuation policy suppressed a genuine degradation — adjusted threshold to require SLO burn velocity > 2x before suppression.
2026-03-05 Product (Marta Liu): Request to expose 'soft-cutover' as an opt-in for Dedicated tenants behind feature flag. Adding to rollout plan.
2026-03-09 Diego Morales: Implemented telemetry dashboard and canary visualizer. Preparing tabletop drills next week.
2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include on-call sign-offs; pushing to in-progress for implementation week
decisions: Decision 2026-02-20: Use 10m default correlation window with exponential backoff for re-correlation (approved by SRE leads)
Decision 2026-02-25: Attenuation default path will downgrade to a low-severity Slack + incident-log rather than fully silent; full suppression requires explicit high-trust condition
Decision 2026-03-03: Soft-cutover will be staged at route-group granularity; global region failover remains manual unless SLO burn rate exceeds emergency threshold
